comment: Geiger hands out 2 opportunities for extra credit that happen at precise times; if you can't make it, he will not give you another chance. Every class, he only goes over random HW problems instead of teaching in a structured manner that makes sense. There's a reason why people generally take him in the spring.. when 301 is only taught by him.

Geiger utilizes the flipped classroom method, so if you do not teach yourself topics easily be prepared to practice. Overall he is a really nice guy and wants his students to learn accounting. He utilizes comedy when teaching and he is not a stickler about cold calling whatsoever. Final grades are how he believes you did, and he values improvement.

Geiger cares a lot about his students and wants everyone to do well. He makes videos to help with homework and to study for tests. It is a hard class by nature, but as long as you do homework and participate, it is not bad. He tries to make accounting fun and engaging.

Insanely nice guy and really good professor. Knows accounting really well, you learn a lot from his lectures. Flipped classroom, so very homework heavy and can be confusing but after listening to him talk about it, everything makes sense. HW, participation, and balance sheet project help boost grade. Talking in class helps a ton. Geiger is goated.
The class is a lot of work, but he cares a lot about his students' success and is definetly a better option than Hoyle.

if you like accounting you will enjoy this class. yes the tests are very hard but if you do all homework problems you will don fine. he offers extra credit and there aren't any quizzes. getting an A is possible. take him over hoyle 100%
shouldve taken hoyle

Geiger for 301 is much easier compared to Hoyle, but get ready to teach yourself. The entirety of class is spent going over homework problems. He does make it pretty easy to get a good grade, as there is a personal balance sheet along with homework and participation grades designed to boost your grade. However, I don't feel like I learned that much

I took Geiger last spring and I was lost for 90% of the time. The flipped class format made it hard to engage with and fully understand the material, and most of class time was spent going over random practice problems. Exams were extremely complicated and some questions were designed to trick you. Gleim practice questions were not helpful.

Great professor. He assigns homework to do before class and goes over the problems in class. There are also some videos to watch that he makes. Great guy and readily available outside of class. Accounting is a hard class but he cares about his students understanding the content.

Very average professor. Lots of homework to be done, and most of the teaching is done in videos outside of class. Try to have some grasp on the concepts before coming to class. Also, getting the Gleim book is highly recommended for the exams.

Geiger is solid. He makes videos for the night before so you don't hear it for the first time in class. Difficult MCQ exams but you can do okay with extra credit. A highlight of the semester was doing the personal balance sheet of your assets which is a decent part of your grade. If you spend a bit of time making it look good, you will do fine.

Dr Geiger wants his students to be very prepared before every class (read textbook, do hw, watch his recorded video) and spends class going through hw. That means class would only be helpful if you are well prepared, otherwise be prepared to teach yourself everything. He does have plenty of extra credit opportunities, which help boost your grade.

He might seems a little arrogant at the beginning, and it is a little hard to go through 201 to 301. However, if you actively participate in class and frequently ask questions after class, you will find it okay to get a good grades. In addition, he gives extra credits for doing homework on time and attending accounting events !

Not sure where the good ratings are coming from to be honest. All he does is ask if anyone has questions on the homeworks and then starts randomly going over practice problems without doing any teaching. Gleim didn't help me at all. Unfortunately he's also the only 301 professor so everyone just has to deal with his class.

I love this man. Such a good guy, and an even better professor. The class revolves around you doing practice problems, which makes sense because that's the best way to learn accounting. Available outside of class and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. Extremely well-respected accounting professional - we are lucky to have him at UR!

Kind of typical bschool class/professor. Cold calls in class sometimes, make sure you come with the problems complete and a basic understanding of the material. Teaches as a flipped classroom style, where you watch videos on some of the assigned problems and go over them in class

Dr. Geiger is one of my favorite professors at UR so far. 301 was a challenging class, but he explained it so well and was more than willing to answer any question. If you do the homework and come to class prepared, it is challenging, but a manageable class. Do the Gleim. Try to get to know him outside of class, he is truly an awesome guy!

Professor Geiger cares about his students but uses all of class time to answer questions and go over homework problems. Office hours are only helpful if you go with very specific questions. Very challenging tests but has a balance sheet project, homework checks, and some extra credit to help boost your grade. DO THE GLEIM PRACTICE.

The class was not hard core at all. The material could be tricky but Geiger handled it very well. Nice guy. Low pressure class. The homework is helpful, and so is reading the textbook. Very fair class; there are no surprises with the hw or tests.

Not a good professor. If I had him freshman year I would have never decided to major in accounting. He is very knowledgeable but a terrible teacher. Class structure is do problems at home and bring questions to the next class. He is not inspiring and doesn't seem to care about his students.

Just ok - class structure was very strange and not really inspiring or motivating. He walks in the class and says "any questions on the hw?" but doesn't demonstrate much of his own teaching ability. It's like if you met with a TA the day before a lecture to go over hw, but surprise! - there is no lecture and you're just firing Q&As for 75 minutes.
Dude loves accounting, very passionate about what he teaches. If you do the homework, participate in class and do the Gleim things there is no way you won't get an A.

Geiger is my favorite teacher at UofR.. I know a lot of people don't say that! But he is so funny, nice, and caring! He always answered my questions, no matter how silly they were. He also has a good sense of humor. His class was really challenging, but it made my 'A' at the end of the semester that much more rewarding.

As someone mentioned earlier: take his class and you will never want to major in accounting again. He is very knowledgable in his subject, but he is just not-a-good-teacher. He doesn't teach you during the class, he only answers questions and goes through a few hwork exercises. Tests consist of the most tricky and hard stuff. DO GLEM EXERCISES.

He is interested in helping you learn and is very helpful with personal balance sheet project if you go to his office. Tests are hard but fair. You have to do the homework and read the book to really follow the lecture in class.

He's the worst professor in bschool I've ever met. When I went to his office hour and asked him questions, he even did not look at me just typing on the computer and saying "i'm listening". He's really unclear in the class and says different things in three sections. HATE HIM!

Please take his class ACCT 301 and you will never think of majoring in Accounting. If you work hard, do every homework, read all the text materials, you probably can get a decent B! Good Luck accounting major students.
I do not like accounting but I like Geiger.  He is funny and fair, and if you study, you can get a B easily.  The A takes a lot of work but is manageable. He is a great though.

Geiger is a nice guy and tries to make class interesting through his occasionally funny jokes. Minimal homework assignments. No quizzes. Final exam is a 3rd test. I struggled at first but eventually got the swing of things. Good teacher overall.
